text:
III. 14. 6-11.] MAHÂVAGGA. 155

. . . he stays within the <term>sannivaṭṭa</term> <gloss>residence or enclosure</gloss> for that seven-day period. For that monk, O monks, the early retreat <note>the *purimikâ*, the first three months of the rainy season retreat</note> is recognized, and there is no offense in the arrival <note>the *paṭissava*</note>. ||6|| But here, if he departs for a duty <note>the *sakaraṇîya*</note> before the <term>pavâraṇâ</term> <gloss>ceremony marking the end of the retreat</gloss> has arrived. Whether that monk returns to that residence or does not return, O monks, for that monk the early retreat is recognized, and there is no offense in the arrival. ||7|| But here, O monks, a retreat has been promised by a monk for the early period. He goes to that residence, performs the <term>uposatha</term> <gloss>observance day</gloss>, approaches the monastery on the day after the Uposatha, arranges the bedding, prepares drinking and usable water, and sweeps the courtyard. He then departs the same day without a duty. For that monk, O monks, the early retreat is not recognized, and there is an offense of wrong-doing <note>the *dukkaṭa*</note> in the arrival. ||8|| But here . . . (= § 8) . . . he departs the same day for a duty — and so on — he stays for two or three days and departs without a duty — and so on — he stays for two or three days and departs for a duty — and so on — he stays for two or three days and departs for a seven-day duty. He spends that seven-day period outside. For that monk, O monks, the early retreat is not recognized, and there is an offense of wrong-doing in the arrival. ||9|| He stays for two or three days and departs for a seven-day duty. He stays within the residence for that seven-day period. For that monk, O monks, the early retreat is recognized, and there is no offense in the arrival. He [stays] for the seven-day period . . . (= § 7) . . . no offense. ||10|| But here, O monks, a retreat has been promised by a monk for the late period <note>the *pacchimikâ*, the second three months of the rainy season retreat</note>. While going to that residence, he performs the <term>uposatha</term> outside, approaches the monastery on the day after the Uposatha, arranges the bedding, prepares drinking and usable water, and sweeps the courtyard. He then departs the same day without a duty. For that monk, O monks, the late retreat is not recognized, and there is an offense of wrong-doing in the arrival. But here . . . (the whole passage is identical with § 5-10; read instead of *purimikâ* and *purimikâya*: *pacchimikâ* and *pacchimikâya*, instead of *anâgatâya pavâraṇâya*: *anâgatâya komudiyâ câtumâsiniyâ* <gloss>before the Komudî full-moon of the four-month season</gloss>) . . . and no offense in the arrival. ||11||14||

vassupanâyikakkhandhako tatiyo.

tassa uddânam:
upagantum, kadâ c’ eva, kati, antarâ vassa ca,
na icchanti ca, sañcicca, ukkaḍḍhitum, upâsako.|

<summary>This page continues the technical regulations for monks observing the rainy season retreat, specifically defining when a retreat is considered valid or invalid based on residency, performance of duties, and timing of the arrival.</summary>
<keywords>Vassa, retreat, monastic discipline, Mahavagga, Vinaya, Dukkaṭa, Uposatha</keywords>

issues.now: on the day after the Uposatha
